title: Working conditions, security and grievance management among Bundibugyo virus response personnel: exploratory findings from an anonymous survey in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
abstract: Abstract Problem Response personnel in the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo work amid protracted conflict and fragile health systems. Working conditions, security exposure and grievance handling were widely reported as sources of stress but had not been documented systematically. Approach We conducted an anonymous, self-administered online survey in French among BVD response personnel in North Kivu, Ituri and South Kivu, covering staffing, EPI supply, remuneration, security incidents, grievances and psychosocial well-being. Of 55 submissions, 54 respondents consented and were analysed; denominators fall further, to 21, for grievance items because of within-survey drop-off. Findings are descriptive. Local setting Respondents (94% men) worked for the Ministry of Health, international non-governmental organizations, the Red Cross and as unpaid volunteers, mostly with one to three months on the response. Relevant changes 61% judged staffing insufficient; 67% had one or no rest day per week. 63% reported EPI stock-outs and 43% had performed a task judged riskier than necessary. 44% had pay delayed, partial or unpaid though promised, and 85% had advanced personal funds for work costs. 67% reported a security incident in three months; among the smaller subgroup reaching the grievance questions, 57% feared reprisal. Lessons learnt Staffing, supply, payment and security shortfalls compound one another and are visible to communities; weak grievance channels and fear of reprisal let them persist unaddressed. Working conditions, security and grievance management should be monitored as core infection-prevention-and-control and occupational-risk indicators, not as a peripheral human-resources matter. What was already known on this topic Previous Ebola epidemics, notably the 2014-2016 West African outbreak, showed that health-worker pay disputes, personal protective equipment shortages and community mistrust can contribute to absenteeism, disengagement and reduced service continuity [2,5,6], and that health workers’ coping depends on training, equipment, a functioning risk allowance and psychosocial support [2]. In eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, repeated Ebola-family outbreaks have occurred alongside armed conflict and institutional distrust [1], but working conditions, security exposure and grievance handling among response personnel are rarely documented systematically during an active response. What this paper adds Using an anonymous survey administered during an ongoing 2026 BVD response, this paper quantifies, in near real time, how response personnel across three eastern DRC provinces experienced staffing, EPI supply, remuneration, security and grievance handling, and how these problems interact. It shows that administrative and security shortfalls are interconnected and visible to communities, and that survey drop-off is itself informative: fewer respondents were willing or able to complete questions on grievances and psychosocial strain than on operational conditions.

abstract_zh: 摘要 问题 在2026年东部刚果民主共和国班杜巴古约病毒病(BVD)暴发应对中,工作人员在长期冲突和脆弱卫生系统环境中工作。工作条件、安全暴露和申诉处理被广泛报告为压力源,但尚未系统记录。方法 我们在北基伍、伊图里和南基伍的BVD应对人员中进行了一项匿名、自我管理的在线法语调查,涵盖人员配置、EPI供应、薪酬、安全事件、申诉和心理社会福祉。共收到55份回复,其中54人同意并被分析;由于调查过程中部分人员退出,申诉相关数据的分母进一步减少至21。研究结果为描述性。当地背景 回应者(94%为男性)主要为卫生部、国际非政府组织、红十字会以及作为无薪志愿者工作,大多数人员参与应对工作的时间为一个月到三个月。相关变化 61%的受访者认为人员配置不足;67%的人每周有1天或没有休息日。63%报告了EPI物资短缺,43%执行了被认为比必要更危险的任务。44%的受访者表示薪酬被延迟、部分支付或未支付,尽管曾承诺支付;85%的受访者曾使用个人资金支付工作相关费用。67%的受访者在三个月内报告了安全事件;在较小的子群体中,57%的人担心遭到报复。经验教训 人员配置、物资供应、薪酬和安全方面的不足相互关联,并对社区可见;薄弱的申诉渠道和对报复的恐惧使这些问题持续存在而未被解决。工作条件、安全和申诉管理应作为核心的感染预防与控制及职业风险指标进行监测,而不仅仅是人力资源方面的次要问题。已有知识 以往的埃博拉病毒病疫情,特别是2014-2016年西非埃博拉病毒病暴发,表明医护人员薪酬纠纷、个人防护装备短缺和社区不信任可能导致缺勤、脱节和医疗服务连续性下降[2,5,6],并且医护人员的应对能力取决于培训、装备、有效的风险津贴和心理社会支持[2]。在东部刚果民主共和国,埃博拉病毒家族的疫情反复发生,伴随着武装冲突和机构不信任[1],但应对人员的工作条件、安全暴露和申诉处理很少在疫情活跃期间被系统记录。本文新增内容 通过在2026年持续的BVD应对期间进行的一项匿名调查,本文近实时地量化了应对人员在三个东部刚果民主共和国省份中对人员配置、EPI供应、薪酬、安全和申诉处理的体验,并展示了这些问题如何相互作用。它表明,行政和安全方面的不足相互关联,并对社区可见,且调查中部分人员退出本身也提供了信息:较少的受访者愿意或能够完成有关申诉和心理社会压力的问题。

title: Notes from the Field: Clinical Characteristics of Patients with Ebola Disease Caused by Bundibugyo Virus - Uganda, 2026.
abstract: Ebola Response Team; Uganda Case Investigation TeamEbola disease is a viral hemorrhagic fever caused by viruses of the genus Orthoebolavirus.Bundibugyo virus (Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense), first identified in 2007 in Bundibugyo District, Uganda, is one of four orthoebolaviruses known to cause Ebola disease in humans (1,2); only two previous Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreaks have been documented (2).Transmission occurs through direct contact with infectious blood or other body fluids (3).Common signs and symptoms include fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea, vomiting, weakness, and bleeding from orifices and injection sites (1).Case-fatality rates (CFRs) among confirmed cases in the two previous outbreaks ranged from 32% to 55% (1,4).No licensed vaccine or specific treatment is available for BVD; clinical management is primarily supportive (2).On May 15, 2026, the Uganda Ministry of Health confirmed an outbreak of BVD imported from the neighboring Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).On August 26, 2026, the outbreak was declared over in Uganda with 20 confirmed BVD cases and one probable case reported, although the outbreak in DRC is ongoing.This report describes the clinical and epidemiologic characteristics of all 21 cases.This activity was reviewed by CDC, deemed not research, and conducted consistent with applicable federal law and CDC policy.* Investigation and Outcomes Index Case and Identification of BVD Outbreak in UgandaThe index patient in Uganda was a man aged 59 years from Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) who traveled to Uganda seeking medical care.He was admitted to a private hospital in Kampala on May 11 with fever, respiratory distress, epigastric pain, and nausea.Despite receiving supportive care, he died in the intensive care unit on May 14.
journal: MMWR. Morbidity and mortality weekly report

source_records.abstract: Ebola Response Team; Uganda Case Investigation TeamEbola disease is a viral hemorrhagic fever caused by viruses of the genus Orthoebolavirus.Bundibugyo virus (Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense), first identified in 2007 in Bundibugyo District, Uganda, is one of four orthoebolaviruses known to cause Ebola disease in humans (1,2); only two previous Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreaks have been documented (2).Transmission occurs through direct contact with infectious blood or other body fluids (3).Common signs and symptoms include fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea, vomiting, weakness, and bleeding from orifices and injection sites (1).Case-fatality rates (CFRs) among confirmed cases in the two previous outbreaks ranged from 32% to 55% (1,4).No licensed vaccine or specific treatment is available for BVD; clinical management is primarily supportive (2).On May 15, 2026, the Uganda Ministry of Health confirmed an outbreak of BVD imported from the neighboring Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).On August 26, 2026, the outbreak was declared over in Uganda with 20 confirmed BVD cases and one probable case reported, although the outbreak in DRC is ongoing.This report describes the clinical and epidemiologic characteristics of all 21 cases.This activity was reviewed by CDC, deemed not research, and conducted consistent with applicable federal law and CDC policy.* Investigation and Outcomes Index Case and Identification of BVD Outbreak in UgandaThe index patient in Uganda was a man aged 59 years from Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) who traveled to Uganda seeking medical care.He was admitted to a private hospital in Kampala on May 11 with fever, respiratory distress, epigastric pain, and nausea.Despite receiving supportive care, he died in the intensive care unit on May 14.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to describe the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of a Bundibugyo virus (BVD) outbreak in Uganda, following an importation from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The outbreak was declared over with 20 confirmed cases and one probable case, highlighting the need for understanding the disease to inform surveillance and management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case investigation was conducted in Uganda, involving 21 cases of BVD, including one index patient who was a man from DRC. The study covered the period from May 15 to August 26, 2026, and included patients from a private hospital in Kampala.
analysis.methods: The study involved clinical case investigations, including patient interviews and medical records review. No specific laboratory or statistical methods were detailed in the provided evidence.
analysis.main_results: The study reported 20 confirmed and one probable case of BVD in Uganda. The index patient died despite supportive care. Common signs and symptoms included fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea, vomiting, weakness, and bleeding. Case-fatality rates among confirmed cases were not explicitly stated.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings to describe the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of BVD, contributing to the understanding of the disease in Uganda. The study highlighted the importance of early detection and supportive care.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and management strategies for BVD, particularly in regions where the virus is endemic or where importations occur. The study underscores the need for continued vigilance and preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the small sample size and the fact that it only covered one outbreak. The lack of specific laboratory or statistical methods reduces the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.main_results: 该研究报告了乌干达20例确诊和1例可能病例的BVD。索引患者尽管接受了支持性治疗仍死亡。常见症状包括发热、腹痛、腹泻、呕吐、乏力和出血。确诊病例的病死率未明确说明。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为监测和BVD的管理策略提供信息,特别是在病毒流行地区或发生输入病例的地区。该研究强调了持续保持警惕和做好准备的必要性。

title_zh: 来自现场的笔记:2026年乌干达由布尼亚圭病毒引起的埃博拉疾病患者的临床特征。
source_body_en: Ebola Response Team; Uganda Case Investigation TeamEbola disease is a viral hemorrhagic fever caused by viruses of the genus Orthoebolavirus.Bundibugyo virus (Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense), first identified in 2007 in Bundibugyo District, Uganda, is one of four orthoebolaviruses known to cause Ebola disease in humans (1,2); only two previous Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreaks have been documented (2).Transmission occurs through direct contact with infectious blood or other body fluids (3).Common signs and symptoms include fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea, vomiting, weakness, and bleeding from orifices and injection sites (1).Case-fatality rates (CFRs) among confirmed cases in the two previous outbreaks ranged from 32% to 55% (1,4).No licensed vaccine or specific treatment is available for BVD; clinical management is primarily supportive (2).On May 15, 2026, the Uganda Ministry of Health confirmed an outbreak of BVD imported from the neighboring Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).On August 26, 2026, the outbreak was declared over in Uganda with 20 confirmed BVD cases and one probable case reported, although the outbreak in DRC is ongoing.This report describes the clinical and epidemiologic characteristics of all 21 cases.This activity was reviewed by CDC, deemed not research, and conducted consistent with applicable federal law and CDC policy.* Investigation and Outcomes Index Case and Identification of BVD Outbreak in UgandaThe index patient in Uganda was a man aged 59 years from Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) who traveled to Uganda seeking medical care.He was admitted to a private hospital in Kampala on May 11 with fever, respiratory distress, epigastric pain, and nausea.Despite receiving supportive care, he died in the intensive care unit on May 14.
abstract_zh: 埃博拉病毒病是一种由埃博拉病毒属病毒引起的病毒性出血热。邦迪布古病毒(Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense)于2007年首次在乌干达邦迪布古区被发现,是已知能引起人类埃博拉病毒病的四种埃博拉病毒之一(1,2);仅有两个先前的邦迪布古病毒病(BVD)暴发病例被记录(2)。传播通过直接接触感染性血液或其他体液传播(3)。常见症状包括发热、腹痛、腹泻、呕吐、乏力以及从孔窍和注射部位出血(1)。在之前记录的两个暴发中,确诊病例的病例死亡率(CFRs)范围为32%至55%(1,4)。目前尚无获批的疫苗或特异性治疗可用于BVD的治疗;临床管理主要是支持性的(2)。2026年5月15日,乌干达卫生部确认了从邻国刚果民主共和国(DRC)输入的BVD 暴发。2026年8月26日,乌干达宣布该暴发结束,共报告了20例确诊BVD病例和1例可能病例,尽管DRC的暴发仍在持续。本报告描述了所有21例病例的临床和流行病学特征。该活动经CDC审查,被认定为非研究性质,并符合适用的联邦法律和CDC政策。* 调查与结果 乌干达BVD 暴发的索引病例及识别索引病例在乌干达的BVD 暴发中,索引病例是一名来自刚果民主共和国(DRC)的59岁男性,他前往乌干达寻求医疗帮助。该患者于2026年5月11日被送往坎帕拉的一家私人医院,主诉为发热、呼吸困难、上腹部疼痛和恶心。尽管接受了支持性治疗,他于2026年5月14日在重症监护室去世。

title: Evidence for cross-reactivity and protection against Bundibugyo virus disease after heterologous vaccination: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: There are currently no approved vaccines or medical countermeasures for use in prevention or treatment of Bundibugyo virus disease. A critical question is whether the existing vaccines approved for use against Ebola virus disease could provide sufficient cross-reactivity and cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus disease. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of published studies of antibody cross-reactivity to Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) after vaccination with previously approved Ebola vaccines (Ervebo or Zabdeno/Mvabea). We find on average a 2.8-fold (95% predictive interval, PI: 2.6-3.0) drop in binding (n = 8 observations from 4 studies) and 3.1-fold drop (95% PI: 2.0-4.8) in neutralization (n = 2 observations from 1 study) between Ebola virus and BDBV antigens after Ervebo vaccination, which appears maintained over time after vaccination. Very limited data on cross reactivity after Zabdeno/Mvabea vaccination suggests a higher drop in recognition of BDBV (39.7-fold, 95% PI: 24.8-63.8; n = 3 observations from 2 studies). In addition to analysis of antibody recognition in humans, we also investigated evidence for vaccine protection from BDBV challenge in animal models after Ervebo or other recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) based vaccines containing only Ebola antigen. A single study in NHP showed non-significant vaccine protection from BDBV challenge, while a study in ferrets showed significant protection after both one and two doses. The available data demonstrate immune cross-reactivity and some evidence for protection in animals, although further clinical and pre-clinical data is urgently needed to inform decisions on the use of Ervebo to protect against Bundibugyo virus disease.

We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of published studies of antibody cross-reactivity to Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) after vaccination with previously approved Ebola vaccines (Ervebo or Zabdeno/Mvabea). We find on average a 2.8-fold (95% predictive interval, PI: 2.6-3.0) drop in binding (n = 8 observations from 4 studies) and 3.1-fold drop (95% PI: 2.0-4.8) in neutralization (n = 2 observations from 1 study) between Ebola virus and BDBV antigens after Ervebo vaccination, which appears maintained over time after vaccination. Very limited data on cross reactivity after Zabdeno/Mvabea vaccination suggests a higher drop in recognition of BDBV (39.7-fold, 95% PI: 24.8-63.8; n = 3 observations from 2 studies). In addition to analysis of antibody recognition in humans, we also investigated evidence for vaccine protection from BDBV challenge in animal models after Ervebo or other recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) based vaccines containing only Ebola antigen. A single study in NHP showed non-significant vaccine protection from BDBV challenge, while a study in ferrets showed significant protection after both one and two doses. The available data demonstrate immune cross-reactivity and some evidence for protection in animals, although further clinical and pre-clinical data is urgently needed to inform decisions on the use of Ervebo to protect against Bundibugyo virus disease.

abstract_zh: 目前,尚未有任何疫苗或医疗对策获得批准,用于预防或治疗邦迪布吉奥病毒病。一个关键问题是,现有的疫苗是否能够提供足够的交叉反应性和交叉保护性,以对抗邦迪布吉奥病毒病。我们对已发表的研究进行了系统回顾和元分析,研究了与此前批准的埃博拉疫苗(Ervebo或Zabdeno/Mvabea)接种后对邦迪布吉奥病毒(BDBV)的抗体交叉反应性。结果显示,在Ervebo接种后,埃博拉病毒和BDBV抗原之间的结合能力平均下降了2.8倍(95%预测区间,PI:2.6-3.0;n=8个观察值,来自4项研究),中和能力下降了3.1倍(95% PI:2.0-4.8;n=2个观察值,来自1项研究),这种下降似乎在疫苗接种后随时间推移而持续存在。关于Zabdeno/Mvabea 疫苗接种后交叉反应的有限数据表明,对BDBV的识别下降幅度更大(39.7倍,95% PI:24.8-63.8;n=3个观察值,来自2项研究)。除了对人类抗体识别的分析外,我们还调查了Ervebo或其他仅含埃博拉抗原的重组囊肿病毒(rVSV)基疫苗在动物模型中对BDBV挑战的保护效果。一项非人灵长类动物研究显示,对BDBV挑战的保护作用不具显著性,而一项雪貂研究则显示,一次和两次接种后均有显著保护效果。现有数据表明存在免疫交叉反应性,并在动物中提供了一些保护证据,但迫切需要进一步的临床和临床前数据,以指导关于使用Ervebo预防邦迪布吉奥病毒病的决策。

title: Detected case growth and outcome heterogeneity during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda
abstract: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with cross-border cases in Uganda, evolved amid mobility, insecurity, delayed detection, laboratory constraints and pressure on case management. We assessed how official aggregate data with documented source provenance could support real-time description of reported case growth, outcome heterogeneity and response constraints. We conducted a retrospective aggregate time-series and subnational ecological analysis of official situation reports and public health updates. The DRC analysis used national, provincial and health-zone data from situation reports 001– 028 covering 14 May–11 June 2026; Uganda was analysed separately through 10 June 2026. Outcomes included epidemic trajectory, growth of reported cumulative confirmed cases, crude observed case-fatality ratios (CFRs) and selected operational indicators. Growth estimates were treated as descriptive measures of reported case accumulation, not direct estimates of transmission intensity. Between 14 May and 11 June 2026, DRC recorded 689 confirmed cases and 139 confirmed deaths across 29 health zones, corresponding to a crude observed CFR of 20.2% (95% CI 17.2–23.4%). Ituri province accounted for 646 cases (93.8%) and had a CFR of 17.6% (95% CI 14.8–20.8%). By 10 June 2026, Uganda had recorded 19 confirmed cases and two confirmed deaths. In the DRC, apparent doubling times were similar during 21–27 May and 4–10 June 2026 (10.5 and 10.3 days, respectively), with a shorter estimate of 7.4 days during 28 May–3 June 2026. Among eligible Ituri health zones, CFRs ranged from 3.0% in Nyankunde to 38.2% in Mongbwalu. Contact follow-up reached 71.8% on 10 June. Ituri test positivity ranged from 26.6% to 68.5% across four reported time points. Official aggregate data from DRC and Uganda during the early 2026 BVD outbreak showed continued accumulation of confirmed cases, geographic expansion, crude outcome heterogeneity and operational constraints in contact follow-up, case management and laboratory turnaround. Phase-specific growth estimates were sensitive to surveillance-series representation and should be interpreted primarily as descriptive measures of reported case accumulation, not direct transmission estimates. Transparent documentation of revisions, unresolved outcomes and subnational data gaps is essential for credible real-time outbreak analysis.

The study aimed to assess how official aggregate data with documented source provenance could support real-time description of reported case growth, outcome heterogeneity, and response constraints.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective aggregate time-series and subnational ecological analysis was conducted using official situation reports and public health updates from the DRC and Uganda during the early 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak.
analysis_en.methods: The analysis used national, provincial, and health-zone data from situation reports covering the period from 14 May to 11 June 2026 for the DRC, and separate analysis for Uganda through 10 June 2026. analysis_en.main_results: Between 14 May and 11 June 2026, the DRC recorded 689 confirmed cases and 139 confirmed deaths across 29 health zones, corresponding to a crude observed CFR of 20.2% (95% CI 17.2–23.4%). Ituri province accounted for 646 cases (93.8%) and had a CFR of 17.6% (95% CI 14.8–20.8%). By 10 June 2026, Uganda had recorded 19 confirmed cases and two confirmed deaths. Apparent doubling times were similar during 21–27 May and 4–10 June 2026 (10.5 and 10.3 days, respectively), with a shorter estimate of 7.4 days during 28 May–3 June 2026. Among eligible Ituri health zones, CFRs ranged from 3.0% in Nyankunde to 38.2% in Mongbwalu. Contact follow-up reached 71.8% on 10 June. Ituri test positivity ranged from 26.6% to 68.5% across four reported time points.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that growth estimates were treated as descriptive measures of reported case accumulation, not direct estimates of transmission intensity. The phase-specific growth estimates were sensitive to surveillance-series representation and should be interpreted primarily as descriptive measures of reported case accumulation, not direct transmission estimates.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and response strategies for future BVD outbreaks. Transparent documentation of revisions, unresolved outcomes, and subnational data gaps is essential for credible real-time outbreak analysis.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the design, which relies on official aggregate data with potential for underreporting and incomplete data. The evidence strength is moderate due to the retrospective nature and the sensitivity of growth estimates to surveillance-series representation.

title_zh: 2026年刚果民主共和国和乌干达本迪布焦病毒病暴发期间检测到的病例增长与结局异质性
source_body_en: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with cross-border cases in Uganda, evolved amid mobility, insecurity, delayed detection, laboratory constraints and pressure on case management. We assessed how official aggregate data with documented source provenance could support real-time description of reported case growth, outcome heterogeneity and response constraints. We conducted a retrospective aggregate time-series and subnational ecological analysis of official situation reports and public health updates. The DRC analysis used national, provincial and health-zone data from situation reports 001– 028 covering 14 May–11 June 2026; Uganda was analysed separately through 10 June 2026. Outcomes included epidemic trajectory, growth of reported cumulative confirmed cases, crude observed case-fatality ratios (CFRs) and selected operational indicators. Growth estimates were treated as descriptive measures of reported case accumulation, not direct estimates of transmission intensity. Between 14 May and 11 June 2026, DRC recorded 689 confirmed cases and 139 confirmed deaths across 29 health zones, corresponding to a crude observed CFR of 20.2% (95% CI 17.2–23.4%). Ituri province accounted for 646 cases (93.8%) and had a CFR of 17.6% (95% CI 14.8–20.8%). By 10 June 2026, Uganda had recorded 19 confirmed cases and two confirmed deaths. In the DRC, apparent doubling times were similar during 21–27 May and 4–10 June 2026 (10.5 and 10.3 days, respectively), with a shorter estimate of 7.4 days during 28 May–3 June 2026. Among eligible Ituri health zones, CFRs ranged from 3.0% in Nyankunde to 38.2% in Mongbwalu. Contact follow-up reached 71.8% on 10 June. Ituri test positivity ranged from 26.6% to 68.5% across four reported time points. Official aggregate data from DRC and Uganda during the early 2026 BVD outbreak showed continued accumulation of confirmed cases, geographic expansion, crude outcome heterogeneity and operational constraints in contact follow-up, case management and laboratory turnaround. Phase-specific growth estimates were sensitive to surveillance-series representation and should be interpreted primarily as descriptive measures of reported case accumulation, not direct transmission estimates. Transparent documentation of revisions, unresolved outcomes and subnational data gaps is essential for credible real-time outbreak analysis.

title: Marburg virus disease: a comprehensive review
abstract: SUMMARY Marburg virus disease (MVD) is a highly fatal illness closely resembling Ebola disease, caused by either Marburg virus (MARV) or Ravn virus (RAVV). It typically begins with a sudden onset of high fever, headache, and malaise, followed by severe gastrointestinal symptoms, bleeding disorders, and, in the most severe cases, multi-organ failure. Case fatality rates vary widely, from 24% up to 90%. MARV and RAVV are zoonotic pathogens, with fruit bats recognized as the main reservoir. Human-to-human transmission generally occurs through direct exposure to infected bodily fluids. Historically, MVD outbreaks were primarily restricted to Central and Eastern Africa. In recent years, however, the disease has appeared in new regions: Ghana recorded its first cases in 2022, followed by concurrent outbreaks in Equatorial Guinea and Tanzania in 2023. Rwanda and Ethiopia experienced their debut outbreaks in 2024 and 2025, respectively, and another outbreak occurred in early 2025 in Tanzania. These incidents point to a troubling rise in annual MVD outbreaks and emphasize the ongoing risk of spillover from wildlife reservoirs and continued human-to-human transmission. Currently, there are no approved vaccines or antiviral treatments for MVD. Patient care focuses on supportive therapies, including aggressive fluid resuscitation, management of blood pressure and circulation, and intensive critical care. Nonetheless, promising countermeasures, such as monoclonal antibodies and antiviral drugs, are advancing through research and clinical trials. Experimental vaccines, particularly those based on viral-vector technologies, have demonstrated robust immune responses and are undergoing human testing. This review provides clinicians with the most recent knowledge of MVD, with a focus on epidemiological patterns, diagnostic procedures, clinical management, and the latest progress in developing medical countermeasures.

title_zh: 马尔堡病毒病:全面综述
source_body_en: SUMMARY Marburg virus disease (MVD) is a highly fatal illness closely resembling Ebola disease, caused by either Marburg virus (MARV) or Ravn virus (RAVV). It typically begins with a sudden onset of high fever, headache, and malaise, followed by severe gastrointestinal symptoms, bleeding disorders, and, in the most severe cases, multi-organ failure. Case fatality rates vary widely, from 24% up to 90%. MARV and RAVV are zoonotic pathogens, with fruit bats recognized as the main reservoir. Human-to-human transmission generally occurs through direct exposure to infected bodily fluids. Historically, MVD outbreaks were primarily restricted to Central and Eastern Africa. In recent years, however, the disease has appeared in new regions: Ghana recorded its first cases in 2022, followed by concurrent outbreaks in Equatorial Guinea and Tanzania in 2023. Rwanda and Ethiopia experienced their debut outbreaks in 2024 and 2025, respectively, and another outbreak occurred in early 2025 in Tanzania. These incidents point to a troubling rise in annual MVD outbreaks and emphasize the ongoing risk of spillover from wildlife reservoirs and continued human-to-human transmission. Currently, there are no approved vaccines or antiviral treatments for MVD. Patient care focuses on supportive therapies, including aggressive fluid resuscitation, management of blood pressure and circulation, and intensive critical care. Nonetheless, promising countermeasures, such as monoclonal antibodies and antiviral drugs, are advancing through research and clinical trials. Experimental vaccines, particularly those based on viral-vector technologies, have demonstrated robust immune responses and are undergoing human testing. This review provides clinicians with the most recent knowledge of MVD, with a focus on epidemiological patterns, diagnostic procedures, clinical management, and the latest progress in developing medical countermeasures.
abstract_zh: 摘要 马尔堡病毒病(MVD)是一种高度致命的疾病,与埃博拉病非常相似,由马尔堡病毒(MARV)或拉瓦病毒(RAVV)引起。它通常以突然的高热、头痛和全身不适开始,随后出现严重的胃肠道症状、出血性疾病,以及在最严重的情况下多器官衰竭。病例死亡率差异很大,从24%到90%不等。MARV和RAVV是人兽共患病病原体,果蝠被认为是主要的储存宿主。人与人之间的传播通常通过直接接触感染者的体液发生。历史上,MVD的暴发主要局限于中非和东非地区。然而,近年来该疾病出现在新的地区:加纳于2022年记录了其首例病例,随后2023年在赤道几内亚和坦桑尼亚同时出现暴发。卢旺达和埃塞俄比亚分别于2024年和2025年首次出现暴发,而另一场暴发则于2025年初在坦桑尼亚发生。这些事件表明MVD的年度暴发数量正在上升,也突显了从野生动物储存宿主和持续的人与人传播中持续存在的风险。目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物或疫苗用于MVD的治疗。患者护理主要集中在支持性治疗上,包括积极的液体复苏、血压和循环管理以及强化的重症监护。尽管如此,一些有前景的应对措施,如单克隆抗体和抗病毒药物,正在研究和临床试验中推进。实验性抗病毒药物,特别是基于病毒基因组技术的药物,已显示出强大的疗效,并正在进行人体试验。本综述为临床医生提供最新的MVD知识,重点包括流行病学模式、诊断程序、临床管理以及最新医学应对措施的发展进展。

title: A Fractional-Order Nonlinear Model for The Transmission Dynamics of Ebola Virus Disease with Quarantine, Vaccination, and Condom Use
abstract: This paper presents a non-linear fractional-order mathematical model for the transmission dynamics of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD), incorporating key control measures such as quarantine, vaccination, and condom use. The model employs fractional calculus to account for memory effects in disease progression and divides the population into relevant epidemiological compartments governed by a system of fractional differential equations. Analytical results, including the derivation of the basic reproduction number and stability analysis of equilibrium points, are used to determine conditions for disease control or persistence. Numerical simulations highlight the influence of the fractional order and demonstrate that the combined implementation of intervention strategies significantly reduces disease spread. The study emphasizes the relevance of fractional-order modeling in capturing realistic dynamics and provides insights for effective EVD control strategies.
journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory

title_zh: 一种用于埃博拉病毒病(埃博拉病毒)传播动态的分数阶非线性模型,包含隔离、疫苗接种和安全套使用
source_body_en: This paper presents a non-linear fractional-order mathematical model for the transmission dynamics of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD), incorporating key control measures such as quarantine, vaccination, and condom use. The model employs fractional calculus to account for memory effects in disease progression and divides the population into relevant epidemiological compartments governed by a system of fractional differential equations. Analytical results, including the derivation of the basic reproduction number and stability analysis of equilibrium points, are used to determine conditions for disease control or persistence. Numerical simulations highlight the influence of the fractional order and demonstrate that the combined implementation of intervention strategies significantly reduces disease spread. The study emphasizes the relevance of fractional-order modeling in capturing realistic dynamics and provides insights for effective EVD control strategies.
abstract_zh: 本文提出了一种非线性的分数阶数学模型,用于描述埃博拉病毒病(埃博拉病毒)的传播动态,纳入了隔离、疫苗接种和安全套使用等关键控制措施。该模型采用分数阶微积分来考虑疾病进展中的记忆效应,并将人口划分为相关的流行病学组分,这些组分由分数阶微分方程组进行描述。分析结果包括基本再生数的推导和平衡点的稳定性分析,用于确定疾病控制或持续的条件。数值模拟突出了分数阶阶数的影响,并表明干预策略的综合实施显著减少了疾病传播。本研究强调了分数阶建模在捕捉现实动态中的相关性,并提供了有效的埃博拉病毒病控制策略的见解。
summary_zh: 本文提出了一种非线性的分数阶数学模型,用于描述埃博拉病毒病(埃博拉病毒)的传播动态,纳入了隔离、疫苗接种和安全套使用等关键控制措施。该模型采用分数阶微积分来考虑疾病进展中的记忆效应,并将人口划分为相关的流行病学组分,这些组分由分数阶微分方程组进行描述。分析结果包括基本再生数的推导和平衡点的稳定性分析,用于确定疾病控制或持续的条件。数值模拟突出了分数阶阶数的影响,并表明干预策略的综合实施显著减少了疾病传播。本研究强调了分数阶建模在捕捉现实动态中的相关性,并提供了有效的埃博拉病毒病控制策略的见解。

title: Local and Global Stability Analysis of the Disease-Free Equilibrium in A Fractional-Order Ebola Virus Transmission Model
abstract: A non-linear fractional-order mathematical model describing the transmission dynamics of Ebola virus disease is developed. The model consists of a system of fourteen non-linear fractional differential equations of order α. The non-negativity of solutions is established, demonstrating that the model is biologically meaningful and mathematically well-posed. The disease-free equilibrium points are derived, and their stability properties are investigated through the construction of appropriate Lyapunov functions. The results show that the disease-free equilibrium points are both locally and globally asymptotically stable. Numerical simulations are performed to illustrate the theoretical results and to further examine the dynamical behavior of the model.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF APPLIED SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY
open_access_pdf: https://iiardjournals.org/get/IJASMT/VOL. 12 NO. 3 2026/Local and Global Stability Analysis 30-48.pdf

title_zh: 无病平衡点在分数阶埃博拉病毒 传播模型中的局部和全局稳定性分析
source_body_en: A non-linear fractional-order mathematical model describing the transmission dynamics of Ebola virus disease is developed. The model consists of a system of fourteen non-linear fractional differential equations of order α. The non-negativity of solutions is established, demonstrating that the model is biologically meaningful and mathematically well-posed. The disease-free equilibrium points are derived, and their stability properties are investigated through the construction of appropriate Lyapunov functions. The results show that the disease-free equilibrium points are both locally and globally asymptotically stable. Numerical simulations are performed to illustrate the theoretical results and to further examine the dynamical behavior of the model.

title: Sub-national heterogeneity in the time-varying reproduction number during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: a hierarchical Bayesian analysis
abstract: National-level estimates of the time-varying reproduction number (Rt) for the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have converged on a value close to the epidemic threshold since early August 2026, consistent with independent joint Bayesian renewal-model estimates. A single national Rt, however, can obscure divergent sub-national epidemic trajectories, particularly across a five-province outbreak in which provinces range from a declining original epicentre to recently-seeded fronts. We estimated Rt at national, provincial, and, where case volume allowed, health-zone level, using both a standard sliding-window (Cori) estimator and a hierarchical Bayesian renewal model with partial pooling across spatial units, fitted by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (No-U-Turn Sampler). Provincial estimates diverged materially from the national trend: as of the week of 6 August 2026, Ituri, the outbreak's original epicentre, had a hierarchical median Rt of 0.91 (95% credible interval [CrI] 0.68 - 1.24), while Nord-Kivu (1.23, [0.87 - 1.72]) and Haut-Uele (1.79, [1.24 - 2.67]) remained above threshold. Health-zone disaggregation, feasible only in Ituri and Nord-Kivu given case volume, showed this provincial picture itself masked further heterogeneity: in Ituri, the zone where the outbreak began (Mongbwalu) had clearly declined (Rt 0.36, [0.17 - 0.74]) while the two largest zones by cumulative case count (Bunia, Rwampara) remained at or above threshold; in Nord-Kivu, elevated transmission was concentrated in a single zone (Katwa, Rt 1.39, [0.85 - 1.99]) while a comparably-sized zone (Butembo) had already declined (0.64, [0.23 - 1.38]). An initial disagreement between the sliding-window and hierarchical provincial estimates was traced to a data-reconstruction artefact (forward-filling, rather than interpolating, multi-day gaps in health-zone reporting) rather than a genuine methods disagreement, and resolved once corrected. The hierarchical model's dispersion structure, calibration, and sensitivity to the generation-interval assumption were each checked explicitly; a shared (non-province-specific) dispersion parameter was retained on the basis of negligible predictive difference (PSIS-LOO), the model achieved 95.0% pooled 95% posterior-predictive interval coverage, and the province ranking was unchanged across a generation-interval sensitivity grid (Spearman {rho} = 1.0). Aggregation masks meaningful heterogeneity in transmission intensity at every spatial resolution examined; response prioritisation based on a single national or even provincial Rt risks directing attention away from the specific zones where transmission remains supercritical.

title_original: Sub-national heterogeneity in the time-varying reproduction number during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: a hierarchical Bayesian analysis

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess sub-national heterogeneity in the time-varying reproduction number (Rt) during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), as national-level estimates may not capture local variations in transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted a hierarchical Bayesian analysis of the 2026 BDBV outbreak across five provinces in the DRC, focusing on estimating Rt at national, provincial, and health-zone levels where sufficient case data was available.
analysis.methods: The researchers used a standard sliding-window estimator and a hierarchical Bayesian renewal model with partial pooling across spatial units, fitted by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (No-U-Turn Sampler) to account for sub-national variations in transmission.
analysis.main_results: Provincial estimates of Rt diverged from the national trend, with Ituri having a median of 0.91 (95% credible interval [CrI] 0.68 - 1.24), Nord-Kivu at 1.23 (0.87 - 1.72), and Haut-Uele at 1.79 (1.24 - 2.67). Health-zone analysis revealed further heterogeneity, with some zones showing declining transmission while others remained above the epidemic threshold.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the importance of sub-national analysis in understanding transmission dynamics, as they reveal significant local variations that a single national estimate might obscure.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform targeted public health interventions by identifying specific zones with ongoing supercritical transmission, allowing for more effective resource allocation and outbreak control strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Aggregation at higher spatial levels may mask important local heterogeneity, and reliance on case volume for health-zone analysis limits the scope of detailed sub-national insights. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study addresses these limitations through explicit model checks and sensitivity analyses.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to assess sub-national heterogeneity in the time-varying reproduction number (Rt). National-level estimates suggested convergence near the epidemic threshold, but provincial estimates revealed significant variation, with some areas still experiencing supercritical transmission. Health-zone analysis further highlighted localized differences, showing that even within provinces, transmission intensity varied. The study used a hierarchical Bayesian renewal model with partial pooling and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo to estimate Rt, addressing limitations in data reporting and model assumptions. The findings emphasize the need for localized surveillance and response strategies to effectively manage outbreaks. However, the study acknowledges that aggregation may obscure important heterogeneity, and the evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess sub-national heterogeneity in the time-varying reproduction number (Rt) during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), as national-level estimates may not capture local variations in transmission.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study conducted a hierarchical Bayesian analysis of the 2026 BDBV outbreak across five provinces in the DRC, focusing on estimating Rt at national, provincial, and health-zone levels where sufficient case data was available.
elements_en.methods: The researchers used a standard sliding-window estimator and a hierarchical Bayesian renewal model with partial pooling across spatial units, fitted by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (No-U-Turn Sampler) to account for sub-national variations in transmission.
elements_en.main_results: Provincial estimates of Rt diverged from the national trend, with Ituri having a median of 0.91 (95% credible interval [CrI] 0.68 - 1.24), Nord-Kivu at 1.23 (0.87 - 1.72), and Haut-Uele at 1.79 (1.24 - 2.67). Health-zone analysis revealed further heterogeneity, with some zones showing declining transmission while others remained above the epidemic threshold.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the importance of sub-national analysis in understanding transmission dynamics, as they reveal significant local variations that a single national estimate might obscure.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform targeted public health interventions by identifying specific zones with ongoing supercritical transmission, allowing for more effective resource allocation and outbreak control strategies.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Aggregation at higher spatial levels may mask important local heterogeneity, and reliance on case volume for health-zone analysis limits the scope of detailed sub-national insights. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study addresses these limitations through explicit model checks and sensitivity analyses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估2026年布尼亚病毒病(BDBV)暴发在刚果民主共和国(DRC)的次国家级异质性,因为国家级估计可能无法捕捉传播的局部变化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究对刚果民主共和国(DRC)五个省份的2026年BDBV 暴发进行了层次贝叶斯分析,重点是在有足够的病例数据的情况下估计国家级、省级和卫生区级别的Rt。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用标准滑动窗口估计器和部分跨空间单位混合贝叶斯更新模型(通过哈密尔顿蒙特卡洛拟合,No-U-Turn采样器),以应对传播的次国家级变化。
elements_zh.main_results: 省级Rt估计值与国家级趋势存在差异,伊图里省的中位数为0.91(95%可信区间[CrI] 0.68 - 1.24),北基伍省为1.23(0.87 - 1.72),上乌埃勒省为1.79(1.24 - 2.67)。卫生区分析揭示了进一步的异质性,一些区传播下降,而其他区仍高于流行病阈值。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了次国家级分析在理解传播动态中的重要性,因为它们揭示了单个国家级估计可能掩盖的显著局部差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以指导针对特定区的公共卫生干预措施,以识别传播仍处于超临界状态的具体区域,从而更有效地分配资源和控制暴发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在较高空间级别上的聚合可能会掩盖重要的局部异质性,而依赖于病例数量进行卫生区分析限制了获得详细的次国家级洞察力。证据强度为中等,通过明确的模型检查和敏感性分析解决了这些限制。

title_zh: 2026年刚果民主共和国 Bundibugyo 病毒病 暴发 疫情中分区域时变繁殖数的异质性:分层贝叶斯分析
source_body_en: National-level estimates of the time-varying reproduction number (Rt) for the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have converged on a value close to the epidemic threshold since early August 2026, consistent with independent joint Bayesian renewal-model estimates. A single national Rt, however, can obscure divergent sub-national epidemic trajectories, particularly across a five-province outbreak in which provinces range from a declining original epicentre to recently-seeded fronts. We estimated Rt at national, provincial, and, where case volume allowed, health-zone level, using both a standard sliding-window (Cori) estimator and a hierarchical Bayesian renewal model with partial pooling across spatial units, fitted by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (No-U-Turn Sampler). Provincial estimates diverged materially from the national trend: as of the week of 6 August 2026, Ituri, the outbreak's original epicentre, had a hierarchical median Rt of 0.91 (95% credible interval [CrI] 0.68 - 1.24), while Nord-Kivu (1.23, [0.87 - 1.72]) and Haut-Uele (1.79, [1.24 - 2.67]) remained above threshold. Health-zone disaggregation, feasible only in Ituri and Nord-Kivu given case volume, showed this provincial picture itself masked further heterogeneity: in Ituri, the zone where the outbreak began (Mongbwalu) had clearly declined (Rt 0.36, [0.17 - 0.74]) while the two largest zones by cumulative case count (Bunia, Rwampara) remained at or above threshold; in Nord-Kivu, elevated transmission was concentrated in a single zone (Katwa, Rt 1.39, [0.85 - 1.99]) while a comparably-sized zone (Butembo) had already declined (0.64, [0.23 - 1.38]). An initial disagreement between the sliding-window and hierarchical provincial estimates was traced to a data-reconstruction artefact (forward-filling, rather than interpolating, multi-day gaps in health-zone reporting) rather than a genuine methods disagreement, and resolved once corrected. The hierarchical model's dispersion structure, calibration, and sensitivity to the generation-interval assumption were each checked explicitly; a shared (non-province-specific) dispersion parameter was retained on the basis of negligible predictive difference (PSIS-LOO), the model achieved 95.0% pooled 95% posterior-predictive interval coverage, and the province ranking was unchanged across a generation-interval sensitivity grid (Spearman {rho} = 1.0). Aggregation masks meaningful heterogeneity in transmission intensity at every spatial resolution examined; response prioritisation based on a single national or even provincial Rt risks directing attention away from the specific zones where transmission remains supercritical.
abstract_zh: 2026年布尼亚病毒病(BDBV)暴发在刚果民主共和国(DRC)的国家级估计表明,自2026年8月初以来,时间变化的再生数(Rt)估计值已接近流行病阈值,与独立的联合贝叶斯更新模型估计结果一致。然而,单一国家级Rt可能掩盖不同地区的流行病轨迹,特别是在包含五个省份的暴发中,这些省份从原始疫区的下降到新出现的前沿不一而足。我们使用标准滑动窗口(Cori)估计器和部分跨空间单位混合贝叶斯更新模型(通过哈密尔顿蒙特卡洛拟合,No-U-Turn采样器)在国家级、省级和允许的情况下在卫生区级别估计Rt。省级估计值与国家级趋势存在实质性差异:截至2026年8月6日那一周,原始疫区伊图里省的混合后中位数Rt为0.91(95%可信区间[CrI] 0.68 - 1.24),而北基伍省(1.23,[0.87 - 1.72])和上乌埃勒省(1.79,[1.24 - 2.67])仍高于阈值。由于病例数量有限,仅在伊图里省和北基伍省进行了卫生区分解,显示了省级图景下的进一步异质性:在伊图里省,暴发开始的地方(蒙加瓦卢)Rt已明显下降(0.36,[0.17 - 0.74]),而累计病例最多的两个区(布尼亚,鲁万帕拉)仍处于或高于阈值;在北基伍省,传播集中在单个区(卡特瓦,Rt 1.39,[0.85 - 1.99]),而一个同样大小的区(布特梅博)已下降(0.64,[0.23 - 1.38])。滑动窗口和省级混合估计之间的初始分歧归因于数据重构伪影(前向填充,而不是插值多日报告中的空白),而不是真正的方法分歧,并在修正后得到解决。混合模型的分散结构、校准和对世代间隔假设的敏感性均得到了明确检查;基于微不足道的预测差异(PSIS-LOO),保留了共享的非省份特定分散参数,模型实现了95.0%的95%后验预测区间覆盖率,并且在世代间隔敏感性网格中省份排名保持不变(Spearman {rho} = 1.0)。聚合可能会在每个空间分辨率下掩盖传播强度的实质性异质性;基于单一国家级或省级Rt的响应优先级可能会将注意力从传播仍处于超临界状态的具体区域转移开。

title: Re-emerging Marburg virus disease in Africa: spillover ecology, geographic expansion, and surveillance vulnerabilities.
abstract: Marburg virus disease (MVD) is re-emerging across Africa as a high-consequence zoonosis shaped by expanding ecological suitability, repeated spillover, and uneven surveillance capacity. This review synthesizes current evidence on the ecological, epidemiological, and operational determinants of contemporary Marburg virus (MARV) emergence. We conceptualize MVD as an ecological-emergence system produced by interactions among reservoir-host biology, environmental change, human exposure, health-system readiness, and mobility, rather than as a series of isolated outbreaks. Recent detections in multiple African regions indicate wider enzootic circulation than previously recognized and support repeated, reservoir-associated introductions from distributed ecological foci. Spillover risk is heightened where mining, land-use change, agricultural encroachment, settlement growth, climate-sensitive habitat disruption, and population movement increase contact with Egyptian rousette bats ( Rousettus aegyptiacus ) and contaminated roost environments. Following primary spillover, diagnostic delays, fragmented surveillance, limited laboratory decentralization, healthcare-associated transmission, and mobility-linked exposure can enable outbreak amplification and delayed recognition. Serological findings further suggest possible "shadow epidemiology," with unrecognized or mild MARV infections occurring outside confirmed outbreak chains. Critical preparedness gaps persist in ecological risk mapping, longitudinal reservoir surveillance, decentralized molecular diagnostics, genomic sequencing, data integration, and cross-border early warning. Future preparedness should move beyond reactive containment toward integrated One Health approach combining predictive ecological surveillance, rapid community-level detection, real-time genomics, infection prevention, risk communication, and regional coordination to identify spillover early and prevent human transmission.

title: Discovering host-viral protein interactions in autophagy: A LIR discovery pipeline for identifying LC3-interacting region motifs in highly virulent viruses.
abstract: Hemorrhagic fever virus (HFV) infections are highly fatal, posing a significant global pandemic threat as they continue to emerge in new locations. HFVs and other highly virulent viruses (HVVs), such as Nipah virus, exploit host cell pathways, including the conserved host autophagy pathway, to promote viral replication. The Atg8/microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3) proteins are necessary for autophagosome formation and maturation. Proteins interact with Atg8-family proteins through LC3-interacting region (LIR) motifs, which is a short linear motif (SLiM) found in intrinsically disordered regions of proteins. The presence of these motifs in viral components suggests they play a role in hijacking or evading the host autophagy pathway, yet the identification of functional LIR motifs in viral proteins remains limited. To address this gap, we developed the LIR Discovery Pipeline (LIR-DP) which integrates amino acid sequence pattern matching, with protein disorder prediction using IUPred3, and modeling with AlphaFold3. Using LIR-DP, we identified 43 putative LIR motifs in 166 proteins from 22 HVVs and predicted that 18 of these LIRs would be functional. In vitro and in cellulo laboratory experiments demonstrated that LIRs from the Marburg virus nucleoprotein, the Nipah virus phosphoprotein, the Ebola virus VP35, and the Rift Valley fever virus NSs protein bind to Atg8/LC3 family proteins. The aromatic amino acid in the first position of each LIR motif was found to be critical for these interactions. We provide evidence for the utility of the LIR-DP in identifying functional LIRs within HVV proteins which may provide valuable insight into the mechanism by which HVVs modulate the autophagy pathway during infection.

title_zh: 发现宿主病毒蛋白在自噬中的相互作用:一种LIR发现管道,用于识别高度致病性病毒中的LC3相互作用区域基序
source_body_en: Hemorrhagic fever virus (HFV) infections are highly fatal, posing a significant global pandemic threat as they continue to emerge in new locations. HFVs and other highly virulent viruses (HVVs), such as Nipah virus, exploit host cell pathways, including the conserved host autophagy pathway, to promote viral replication. The Atg8/microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3) proteins are necessary for autophagosome formation and maturation. Proteins interact with Atg8-family proteins through LC3-interacting region (LIR) motifs, which is a short linear motif (SLiM) found in intrinsically disordered regions of proteins. The presence of these motifs in viral components suggests they play a role in hijacking or evading the host autophagy pathway, yet the identification of functional LIR motifs in viral proteins remains limited. To address this gap, we developed the LIR Discovery Pipeline (LIR-DP) which integrates amino acid sequence pattern matching, with protein disorder prediction using IUPred3, and modeling with AlphaFold3. Using LIR-DP, we identified 43 putative LIR motifs in 166 proteins from 22 HVVs and predicted that 18 of these LIRs would be functional. In vitro and in cellulo laboratory experiments demonstrated that LIRs from the Marburg virus nucleoprotein, the Nipah virus phosphoprotein, the Ebola virus VP35, and the Rift Valley fever virus NSs protein bind to Atg8/LC3 family proteins. The aromatic amino acid in the first position of each LIR motif was found to be critical for these interactions. We provide evidence for the utility of the LIR-DP in identifying functional LIRs within HVV proteins which may provide valuable insight into the mechanism by which HVVs modulate the autophagy pathway during infection.
abstract_zh: 出血热病毒(HFV)感染具有高致死率,构成了严重的全球疫情威胁,因为它们不断在新的地区出现。HFV 和其他高致病性病毒(HVV),如尼帕病毒,利用 宿主 细胞途径(包括保守的 宿主 自噬途径)来促进病毒复制。Atg8/微管相关蛋白 1 轻链 3(LC3)蛋白对于自噬泡的形成和成熟至关重要。蛋白质通过 LC3 相互作用区域(LIR)基序与 Atg8 家族蛋白相互作用,LIR 基序是蛋白质中不可溶区域发现的一种短线性基序(SLiM)。病毒成分中存在这些基序,表明它们可能在劫持或逃避 宿主 自噬途径中发挥作用,但病毒蛋白中功能性 LIR 基序的识别仍然有限。为了填补这一空白,我们开发了 LIR 发现管道(LIR-DP),该管道集成了氨基酸序列模式匹配、IUPred3 蛋白质无序性预测和 AlphaFold3 建模技术。使用 LIR-DP,我们在 22 种 HVV 的 166 种蛋白中发现了 43 个潜在的 LIR 基序,并预测其中 18 个 LIR 是功能性的。体外和细胞内实验室实验表明,马尔堡病毒核蛋白、尼帕病毒磷蛋白、埃博拉病毒 VP35 和裂谷热病毒 NSs 蛋白的 LIR 能够与 Atg8/LC3 家族蛋白结合。每个 LIR 基序中第一个位置的芳香族氨基酸对这些相互作用至关重要。我们提供了证据,证明 LIR-DP 在识别 HVV 蛋白中功能性 LIR 方面的有效性,这可能为 HVV 在感染期间如何调节自噬途径提供宝贵的见解。

title: Evaluating the 7-1-7 Outbreak Response Metric: Modelling and Implementation Insights for Ebola, Measles, and Anthrax in Central and Eastern Uganda, 2025
abstract: Introduction: Uganda’s recent progress in public health emergency preparedness underscores the relevance of the 7–1-7 framework (detection within 7 days, notification within 1 day, response within 7 days). Evidence on the incremental benefits of meeting these targets in resource-constrained settings remains limited. We modelled cases averted and cost-effectiveness of achieving 7–1-7 timelines for Sudan virus disease (SVD), measles, and anthrax in Uganda, and additionally explored more ambitious targets (3–1-4 and 1–1-1). Methods We used stochastic compartmental models to compare observed response time lines with hypothetical scenarios that meet 7–1-7 targets. Surveillance data from recent outbreaks informed the models. Cost-effectiveness was assessed using Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) averted and Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratios (ICERs). Additional simulations tested the impact of compressing timelines to 3–1-4 and 1–1-1 while keeping all other intervention parameters identical. Results Under the modelled 7–1-7 scenario, 133 SVD cases (47 deaths) and 1,409 DALYs would be averted, with an ICER of −17.46 USD/DALY (cost-saving). For measles, 81 cases and one death would be averted (ICER 83 USD/DALY). For anthrax, the framework would prevent three human cases (one death) and 50 animal cases (45 animal deaths), averting 734 DALYs, but would require an additional US$651,811 for livestock vaccination and carcass disposal. All ICERs fell below Uganda’s willingness-to-pay threshold (1,300 USD/DALY). Moving beyond 7–1-7 to 1–1-1 would avert an additional 55 SVD cases and 21 deaths, and 13 measles cases, at negligible incremental cost, demonstrating that even faster response yields substantial extra health gains. For anthrax, faster timelines beyond 7–1-7 produced only marginal benefits, confirming that vaccination coverage – not timeliness – is the dominant driver. Conclusion The 7–1-7 framework substantially reduces cases, deaths, and costs across three diverse diseases. Accelerating to 1–1-1 further amplifies these benefits for fast-spreading pathogens like Ebola and measles, but for slow zoonoses like anthrax, improving vaccination coverage remains paramount. Achieving these targets requires investments in rapid detection, contact tracing, vaccination, referral systems, and sustainable multi-sector financing.

title_zh: 评估7-1-7 暴发响应指标:乌干达中部和东部地区埃博拉病毒、麻疹和炭疽病的建模与实施洞察,2025年
source_body_en: Introduction: Uganda’s recent progress in public health emergency preparedness underscores the relevance of the 7–1-7 framework (detection within 7 days, notification within 1 day, response within 7 days). Evidence on the incremental benefits of meeting these targets in resource-constrained settings remains limited. We modelled cases averted and cost-effectiveness of achieving 7–1-7 timelines for Sudan virus disease (SVD), measles, and anthrax in Uganda, and additionally explored more ambitious targets (3–1-4 and 1–1-1). Methods We used stochastic compartmental models to compare observed response time lines with hypothetical scenarios that meet 7–1-7 targets. Surveillance data from recent outbreaks informed the models. Cost-effectiveness was assessed using Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) averted and Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratios (ICERs). Additional simulations tested the impact of compressing timelines to 3–1-4 and 1–1-1 while keeping all other intervention parameters identical. Results Under the modelled 7–1-7 scenario, 133 SVD cases (47 deaths) and 1,409 DALYs would be averted, with an ICER of −17.46 USD/DALY (cost-saving). For measles, 81 cases and one death would be averted (ICER 83 USD/DALY). For anthrax, the framework would prevent three human cases (one death) and 50 animal cases (45 animal deaths), averting 734 DALYs, but would require an additional US$651,811 for livestock vaccination and carcass disposal. All ICERs fell below Uganda’s willingness-to-pay threshold (1,300 USD/DALY). Moving beyond 7–1-7 to 1–1-1 would avert an additional 55 SVD cases and 21 deaths, and 13 measles cases, at negligible incremental cost, demonstrating that even faster response yields substantial extra health gains. For anthrax, faster timelines beyond 7–1-7 produced only marginal benefits, confirming that vaccination coverage – not timeliness – is the dominant driver. Conclusion The 7–1-7 framework substantially reduces cases, deaths, and costs across three diverse diseases. Accelerating to 1–1-1 further amplifies these benefits for fast-spreading pathogens like Ebola and measles, but for slow zoonoses like anthrax, improving vaccination coverage remains paramount. Achieving these targets requires investments in rapid detection, contact tracing, vaccination, referral systems, and sustainable multi-sector financing.
abstract_zh: 引言:乌干达在公共卫生紧急事件准备方面的最新进展凸显了7–1-7框架(7天内检测、1天内通报、7天内响应)的相关性。目前关于在资源有限环境中实现这些目标的增量效益的证据仍然有限。我们对乌干达实现7–1-7时间线的SVD(苏丹病毒病)、麻疹和炭疽病例数和成本效益进行了建模,并进一步探讨了更具雄心的目标(3–1-4和1–1-1)。方法:我们使用随机的分室模型,将观察到的响应时间线与假设符合7–1-7目标的场景进行比较。近期监测数据用于模型构建。成本效益评估采用避免的伤残调整生命年(DALYs)和增量成本效益比(ICERs)。此外,我们进行了额外的模拟,测试将时间线压缩至3–1-4和1–1-1时,其他干预参数保持不变的情况下所产生的影响。结果:在模拟的7–1-7情景下,可避免133例SVD病例(47例死亡)和1,409个DALYs,其ICER为−17.46 USD/DALY(成本节约)。对于麻疹,可避免81例病例和1例死亡(ICER 83 USD/DALY)。对于炭疽病,该框架可防止3例人类病例(1例死亡)和50例动物病例(45例动物死亡),避免734个DALYs,但需要额外651,811美元用于牲畜疫苗接种和尸体处理。所有ICER均低于乌干达的意愿支付阈值(1,300 USD/DALY)。超越7–1-7框架,采用1–1-1框架可额外避免55例SVD病例和21例死亡,以及13例麻疹病例,其增量成本微乎其微,表明即使更快的响应也能带来显著的额外健康收益。对于炭疽病,更快的时间线仅产生有限的效益,证实了疫苗接种覆盖率——而非响应速度——是主要驱动因素。结论:7–1-7框架在三种不同的疾病中显著减少了病例、死亡和成本。对于传播迅速的病原体如埃博拉病毒和麻疹,加速至1–1-1框架可进一步放大这些效益,但对于传播较慢的人兽共患病如炭疽病,提高疫苗接种覆盖率仍然是关键。实现这些目标需要在快速检测、接触追踪、疫苗接种、转诊系统和可持续的多部门资金投入方面进行投资。

title: MHRN Roundtable Report: Social and Behavioural Science Priorities for Ebola Clinical Trials in DRC
abstract: A large outbreak of the Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) was first identified in the Ituri Province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in May 2026. This marked the DRC’s 17th Ebola outbreak overall and only the third known outbreak of this virus since its identification in Uganda in 2007. There are currently no licensed vaccines or therapeutics for BDBV, though several trials are planned and underway. DRC has been at the centre of major experimental Ebola vaccine, and therapeutic and diagnostic research over the past decade. Experience from the outbreak in North Kivu in 2018–20, the DRC-EB-001 trial of the Janssen two-dose vaccine, and more recent mpox vaccine trials has generated important lessons about rumour, mistrust, participant experience, protocol change, and the inclusion of vulnerable groups. A growing body of social science research shows that social and behavioural science (SBS) and risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) can strengthen trial operations when they are integrated from the beginning. This includes improving design and implementation, reducing the risk of coercion or misunderstanding, supporting local ethical deliberation, and identifying contextual factors that may otherwise undermine feasibility, recruitment, retention, and trust. Against this backdrop, the Multi-Hazard Research Network (MHRN) organised an online roundtable on 18 August 2026. The aim was to consolidate lessons learned from past SBS research in/on Ebola clinical trials and discuss current challenges with clinical trial design and rollout. The discussion brought together SBS researchers, trial implementers, RCCE specialists, and Ebola responders.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for integrating social and behavioural science (SBS) and risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) into Ebola clinical trials to improve their design and implementation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a roundtable discussion held on 18 August 2026 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), bringing together SBS researchers, trial implementers, RCCE specialists, and Ebola responders.
analysis.methods: The methods involved a structured online roundtable discussion to consolidate lessons learned from past SBS research in Ebola clinical trials and to discuss current challenges with trial design and rollout.
analysis.main_results: The discussion highlighted important lessons from past outbreaks, including the impact of rumour, mistrust, participant experience, protocol changes, and the inclusion of vulnerable groups.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as demonstrating the value of integrating SBS and RCCE from the beginning of clinical trials to enhance their effectiveness and address contextual challenges.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform future Ebola clinical trials by emphasizing the importance of incorporating social and behavioural insights to improve feasibility, recruitment, retention, and trust.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a discussion format and does not include empirical data, but the evidence is strong due to the integration of multiple expert perspectives and prior research findings.

analysis.summary_en: This report outlines the importance of integrating social and behavioural science (SBS) and risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) into Ebola clinical trials. It highlights the need for these approaches to address challenges such as mistrust, rumour, and the inclusion of vulnerable groups, based on lessons from past outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The study was a roundtable discussion held on 18 August 2026, involving SBS researchers, trial implementers, RCCE specialists, and Ebola responders. The findings suggest that incorporating SBS and RCCE from the outset can improve trial design and implementation. The report emphasizes the significance of these insights for future Ebola trials, particularly in enhancing feasibility and trust. However, the study is limited to a discussion format and lacks empirical data, which may affect the strength of the evidence. The confidence in the findings is moderate due to the nature of the evidence and the absence of quantitative results.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是在刚果民主共和国(DRC)于2026年8月18日举行的一次圆桌会议,汇集了社会与行为科学研究人员、试验实施人员、风险沟通与社区参与专家以及埃博拉应对人员。

elements_zh.main_results: 讨论强调了过去疫情中的重要经验教训,包括谣言、不信任、参与者体验、方案变更以及脆弱群体纳入的影响。

analysis_en.methods: The methods involved a structured online roundtable discussion to consolidate lessons learned from past SBS research in Ebola clinical trials and to discuss current challenges with trial design and rollout.
analysis_en.main_results: The discussion highlighted important lessons from past outbreaks, including the impact of rumour, mistrust, participant experience, protocol changes, and the inclusion of vulnerable groups.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as demonstrating the value of integrating SBS and RCCE from the beginning of clinical trials to enhance their effectiveness and address contextual challenges.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform future Ebola clinical trials by emphasizing the importance of incorporating social and behavioural insights to improve feasibility, recruitment, retention, and trust.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a discussion format and does not include empirical data, but the evidence is strong due to the integration of multiple expert perspectives and prior research findings.

title_zh: MHRN圆桌会议报告:刚果民主共和国埃博拉临床试验中的社会与行为科学优先事项
source_body_en: A large outbreak of the Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) was first identified in the Ituri Province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in May 2026. This marked the DRC’s 17th Ebola outbreak overall and only the third known outbreak of this virus since its identification in Uganda in 2007. There are currently no licensed vaccines or therapeutics for BDBV, though several trials are planned and underway. DRC has been at the centre of major experimental Ebola vaccine, and therapeutic and diagnostic research over the past decade. Experience from the outbreak in North Kivu in 2018–20, the DRC-EB-001 trial of the Janssen two-dose vaccine, and more recent mpox vaccine trials has generated important lessons about rumour, mistrust, participant experience, protocol change, and the inclusion of vulnerable groups. A growing body of social science research shows that social and behavioural science (SBS) and risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) can strengthen trial operations when they are integrated from the beginning. This includes improving design and implementation, reducing the risk of coercion or misunderstanding, supporting local ethical deliberation, and identifying contextual factors that may otherwise undermine feasibility, recruitment, retention, and trust. Against this backdrop, the Multi-Hazard Research Network (MHRN) organised an online roundtable on 18 August 2026. The aim was to consolidate lessons learned from past SBS research in/on Ebola clinical trials and discuss current challenges with clinical trial design and rollout. The discussion brought together SBS researchers, trial implementers, RCCE specialists, and Ebola responders.
abstract_zh: 2026年5月,刚果民主共和国(DRC)的伊图里省首次发现了邦迪布古埃博拉病毒(BDBV)的大规模暴发。这标志着DRC自2007年该病毒在乌干达被鉴定以来的第17次埃博拉病毒暴发,也是该病毒第三次已知的暴发。目前尚无针对BDBV的获批抗病毒药物或治疗药物,尽管已有多个试验计划并正在进行中。过去十年中,DRC一直是重大实验性埃博拉病毒药物、治疗和诊断研究的中心。从2018–20年北基伏地区的暴发、DRC-EB-001试验中詹森双剂量疫苗的试验,以及最近的猴痘病毒试验中获得的经验,为理解谣言、不信任、参与者体验、方案变更以及脆弱群体的纳入提供了重要启示。越来越多的社会科学研究表明,当社会和行为科学(SBS)和风险沟通与社区参与(RCCE)从一开始就整合到试验中时,可以增强试验的运行效果。这包括改进试验设计和实施,降低胁迫或误解的风险,支持本地伦理讨论,并识别可能影响试验可行性、招募、保留和信任的背景因素。在此背景下,多灾害研究网络(MHRN)于2026年8月18日组织了一次在线圆桌会议。会议旨在总结过去埃博拉临床试验中社会行为科学研究的经验,并讨论当前临床试验设计和实施中的挑战。讨论汇集了社会行为科学研究人员、试验实施人员、风险沟通与社区参与专家以及埃博拉应对人员。
summary_zh: 2026年5月,刚果民主共和国(DRC)的伊图里省首次发现了邦迪布古埃博拉病毒(BDBV)的大规模暴发。这标志着DRC自2007年该病毒在乌干达被鉴定以来的第17次埃博拉病毒暴发,也是该病毒第三次已知的暴发。目前尚无针对BDBV的获批抗病毒药物或治疗药物,尽管已有多个试验计划并正在进行中。过去十年中,DRC一直是重大实验性埃博拉病毒药物、治疗和诊断研究的中心。从2018–20年北基伏地区的暴发、DRC-EB-001试验中詹森双剂量疫苗的试验,以及最近的猴痘病毒试验中获得的经验,为理解谣言、不信任、参与者体验、方案变更以及脆弱群体的纳入提供了重要启示。越来越多的社会科学研究表明,当社会和行为科学(SBS)和风险沟通与社区参与(RCCE)从一开始就整合到试验中时,可以增强试验的运行效果。这包括改进试验设计和实施,降低胁迫或误解的风险,支持本地伦理讨论,并识别可能影响试验可行性、招募、保留和信任的背景因素。在此背景下,多灾害研究网络(MHRN)于2026年8月18日组织了一次在线圆桌会议。会议旨在总结过去埃博拉临床试验中社会行为科学研究的经验,并讨论当前临床试验设计和实施中的挑战。讨论汇集了社会行为科学研究人员、试验实施人员、风险沟通与社区参与专家以及埃博拉应对人员。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决将社会与行为科学(SBS)和风险沟通与社区参与(RCCE)整合到埃博拉临床试验中的需求,以提高试验的设计和实施效果。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是在刚果民主共和国(DRC)于2026年8月18日举行的一次圆桌会议,汇集了社会与行为科学研究人员、试验实施人员、风险沟通与社区参与专家以及埃博拉应对人员。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究方法包括一次结构化的在线圆桌会议,以总结过去在埃博拉临床试验中的社会与行为科学研究经验,并讨论当前试验设计和实施中的挑战。
analysis_zh.main_results: 讨论强调了过去疫情中的重要经验教训,包括谣言、不信任、参与者体验、方案变更以及脆弱群体纳入的影响。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为表明,从临床试验开始阶段就整合社会与行为科学(SBS)和风险沟通与社区参与(RCCE)对于提高试验效果和应对背景挑战具有重要价值。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为未来的埃博拉临床试验提供信息,强调将社会与行为科学见解纳入其中对于提高可行性、招募、保留和信任的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于讨论形式,不包含实证数据,但由于整合了多种专家观点和以往研究结果,其证据是强有力的。

title: Lassa Virus—A Persistent and Evolving Threat
abstract: Lassa virus (LASV), the most important human pathogen within the Arenaviridae family, causes Lassa fever (LF), an acute hemorrhagic fever disease endemic in West Africa with high case fatality rates, particularly in pregnant women. Currently, there are no licensed vaccines or antivirals approved for clinical use against LASV infection. Despite its significant impact on public health, important knowledge gaps remain regarding LASV disease burden, transmission dynamics, pathogenesis, and virus−host interactions, impeding effective disease control and development of therapeutic interventions. title: Optimal control metapopulation models for the West Africa Ebola epidemic and their nonstandard finite difference discretizations
abstract: The 2014-2016 Ebola Virus disease (EVD) outbreak came with an unprecedented challenge. It simultaneously arose in three different countries with considerable inbound and outbound travels. This led the World Health Organization (WHO) to suggest implementing exit screening of travelers at their borders. In addition to this measure, some countries accounted for entry screening and/or vaccination to curb the disease. In this paper, we consider two optimal controls for patch models in which other interventions supplement exit screening. The first problem is defined through the exit and entry screenings of travelers. The second involves the combination of exit screening and vaccination interventions. We prove the well-posedness of both optimal control problems. For each problem, we construct a new Nonstandard Finite Difference Forward-Backward-Sweep-Method, which preserves the dynamics of the continuous model. Numerical simulations that support the theory are provided. They also suggest that vaccination alone is effective in reducing the disease burden.

title: First mRNA‐based flu vaccine wins US approval, Moderna’s Ebola candidate reaches the clinic, and early‐phase cancer vaccine trials broaden across personalized and off‐the‐shelf platforms
abstract: The US FDA approved the first mRNA-based influenza vaccine, clearing the way for messenger RNA technology to move into a second major indication beyond COVID-19, while Moderna dosed the first participants in its own mRNA candidate against Bundibugyo ebolavirus as the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continued. Mpox vaccine access widened to children as young as two in the European Union, a six-valent Lyme disease vaccine advanced toward EU review, and a cluster of early-phase trials opened for personalized and off-the-shelf cancer vaccine candidates spanning lung, breast, esophagogastric, and pancreatic cancer.

title: Retrieval-Guided Transfer Learning for Low-Resource Ebola Drug–Target Affinity Prediction
abstract: Drug–target affinity (DTA) prediction plays an important role in computational drug discovery; however, its application to emerging infectious diseases such as Ebola remains challenging because of the limited availability of experimentally measured affinity data. To address this low-resource setting, we propose a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework that leverages BindingDB interactions to improve Ebola DTA prediction. The framework uses a two-stage strategy. In Stage I, source interactions are selected using random sampling, compound-similarity retrieval, protein-similarity retrieval, or hybrid compound–protein retrieval at source-data budgets of 50,000 and 300,000 interactions and combined with Ebola training data to learn transferable representations. In Stage II, the pretrained compound and protein encoders are frozen, while the prediction layers are adapted to the Ebola domain. The framework was implemented with DeepDTA and GraphDTA and evaluated across five random seeds using a scaffold-based split, with conventional machine-learning models and single-stage deep learning as baselines. The best overall configuration, GraphDTA with protein-similarity-guided retrieval at the 50,000-interaction budget, achieved RMSE =0.5498±0.1073, R2=0.8809±0.0452, and Pearson =0.9395±0.0237, outperforming the strongest conventional machine-learning model (Extra Trees, RMSE =0.6065±0.0642) and single-stage GraphDTA (RMSE =0.6533±0.0752). Across both source-data budgets and both DTA backbones, all targeted retrieval configurations achieved lower mean RMSE than their corresponding random-retrieval configurations. At the 50,000-interaction budget, matched seed-wise analysis further showed consistent improvements for protein-guided retrieval across all five seeds for both backbones. Retrieval characterization showed stronger target-domain similarity and substantially lower cross-strategy overlap at 50,000 than at 300,000 interactions, while post hoc sequence analysis independently confirmed enrichment of sequence-level relatedness with protein-guided retrieval. Increasing the source-data budget from 50,000 to 300,000 did not uniformly improve predictive performance, indicating that source-data relevance and retrieval selectivity should be considered jointly with source-data quantity. Finally, virtual-screening and approved-drug repurposing case studies across six Ebola virus targets demonstrate the use of the framework for computational prioritization of compound–target hypotheses. Overall, the findings support relevance-guided source-data selection as an effective strategy for transfer learning in low-resource DTA prediction.

title: Healthcare system disruption across WHO-declared PHEICs: a 4S comparative case analysis
abstract: Objectives To compare documented patterns of healthcare-system disruption and response across WHO-declared Public Health Emergencies of International Concern (PHEICs) using the established 4S surge-capacity framework (Staff, Stuff, Space, Systems) and an author-developed 12-indicator operationalization. Methods We conducted a structured comparative case analysis, not a systematic review of intervention effects, of all eight PHEIC events declared by WHO through 31 March 2026. The unit of analysis was the event, and the coded observations were operational occurrences documented in official sources. Twelve binary, unweighted author-developed indicators, three per 4S domain, were mapped to the four established domains. Activation required either one primary official source or two independent secondary sources meeting a prespecified threshold. Two reviewers independently assigned indicator-level codes, with disagreements resolved by consensus; indicators classified as Not Reported were combined with Not Activated. Activated indicators were summed within domains (range 0–3), and each observed configuration was assigned to one of four profiles using a fixed hierarchical rule sequence. Results All eight events activated at least one indicator, and external workforce mobilization (S1) and diagnostic bottleneck (T3) were documented in every event. COVID-19 was the only event activating all 12 indicators (systemic convergence). The two Ebola virus disease events shared an identical configuration of complete Staff, Stuff, and Systems activation with Space limited to temporary or repurposed facilities (workforce-cascade). H1N1 influenza, poliomyelitis, and mpox clade I formed the residual partial multi-domain category and did not share a common domain signature. Zika virus disease and mpox clade II met the limited-domain rule, with no Space-domain activation. Conclusion Public Health Emergencies of International Concern designation was not sufficient to identify a common pattern of documented health-system disruption. The typology is a provisional descriptive partition rather than a severity ranking, causal model, or predictive tool, and its residual category is heterogeneous by construction. Profiles are conditional on the documentary evidence base and the settings it represents; baseline health-system capacity was not incorporated, so the same pathogen could plausibly yield a different configuration elsewhere. The framework may offer a common vocabulary for discussing domain-specific preparedness needs under the revised International Health Regulations and the developing WHO Pandemic Agreement, but external validation is required.

title: An Approximate Solution of a Fractional-Order Epidemic Model Using the Homotopy Perturbation Method
abstract: Ebola virus disease is a highly infectious and life-threatening illness that poses a major public health challenge. In this study, a fractional-order Ebola virus transmission model is developed to describe the spread of the disease within a population. The model uses fractional differential equations to incorporate memory effects in the transmission dynamics. Because the resulting system is nonlinear and difficult to solve exactly, the homotopy perturbation method (HPM) is applied to obtain approximate analytical solutions. Numerical simulations are presented to illustrate the behavior of the model and to examine the influence of the semi-analytical method on disease spread. The results show that the homotopy perturbation method is an effective technique for solving fractional epidemic models and provides useful insights into Ebola virus transmission dynamics.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF APPLIED SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY

title: An Optimal Control Study of Ebola Transmission Incorporating Enlightenment and Drug Effectiveness
abstract: This study presents a mathematical model for the transmission dynamics of Ebola virus disease, incorporating two key control strategies: public enlightenment and drug effectiveness. Using optimal control theory, the effect of these interventions on the spread of the disease was analyzed and conditions under which the spread can be significantly reduced were identified. Basic properties of the model were analyzed and optimal control method using enlightenment and drug effectiveness as controls in the model was used to determine how to manage the spread of the disease. Numerical simulations with control measures and without control were carried out. Our results demonstrate that enlightenment campaigns which include public awareness, hygiene practices, and early reporting play a critical role in reducing the contact rate and enhancing community response. When applied optimally, these strategies significantly reduce the number of infected individuals over time. Similarly, the inclusion of drug effectiveness in the model, representing therapeutic interventions or supportive care, shows a marked decrease in both infection and death rates when optimally applied. The results obtained showed that the spread of the disease could be considerably reduced with drug effectiveness and enlightenment of the populace about the risk factors involved.
journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
